notes: rounds/tester.py record_result checks the round is Open and the build current for GET and again under the round lock for POST, reads the tester's result through own_result (filtered by author) and refuses a POST to a submitted one; services.record_result fetches the row by author again and raises ResultSubmitted, and result.html shows a submitted result without a form and hard-codes 'Status: Draft' in the form branch. M1 drops the author filter in both reads; M3 lets both Open checks pass a Closed round; M4 removes the view and service checks, shows the form for a submitted result and prints its real status there. ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint); M5 raises only ObservationField's max_length, so its message still says 2000. M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005_result to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
